# **Federated Infrastructure and Reproducibility Architecture for the nectR Multi-Hive Blockchain**

> **Notice:** This document is an AI-generated Deep Research report (synthesized using Gemini Deep Research) serving as foundational reference material. Key mechanisms and citations are mapped into nectR's specifications, but claims should be cross-referenced with primary peer-reviewed sources.

For a lightweight, federated multi-hive PoUW-PoW campus blockchain (nectR) deployed on standard university VMs and reproducible academic testbeds, the strongest permissive open-source architecture pairs **NATS Server with Leaf Nodes and JetStream Domains (nats-py)** for cross-hive proof federation, **RocksDict** (or single-writer **aiosqlite** in strict WAL snapshot mode) for deterministic embedded state storage, **Kurtosis** (post-June-2024 Apache-2.0 releases) alongside **Pumba** and **Toxiproxy** for fault-injected devnets, and **OpenTelemetry Python \+ Prometheus \+ Perses** for empirical telemetry. This stack integrates directly with nectR's existing asyncio-based HiveServiceLayer (fastapi, uvicorn, httpx) behind hexagonal ports and adapters without introducing GPU/ASIC mining requirements or incompatible async runtimes.  
Three technical and licensing boundaries shape this design. First, although py-libp2p reached v0.8.0 in September 2026 with persistent keystores and pub/sub readiness barriers, it migrated exclusively to trio and removed asyncio support, preventing direct in-process embedding inside uvicorn/FastAPI workers without sidecar isolation1. Second, strict MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD hygiene requires replacing Grafana—whose license was not verified as permissive in the collected sources—with **Perses** (explicitly Apache-2.0 across all components) and pinning post-June-2024 Apache-2.0 **Kurtosis** releases rather than earlier BSL artifacts3. Third, no independent empirical benchmarks comparing RocksDict against aiosqlite/py-lmdb, networkx graph projections, k3s versus Docker Compose footprints, gRPC/HTTP2 gossip, or PyArrow/Parquet export latency were available in the surveyed sources; accordingly, all storage, graph-telemetry, and export modules sit behind swappable hexagonal ports.

## **Reference Federated Multi-Hive Architecture**

A federated 2+ Hive nectR deployment (HIVE\_A, HIVE\_B, and optional relay or observer nodes) separates consensus-critical state transitions from off-chain Knowledge Graph analytics and cross-campus message transport. Each university campus operates an autonomous Hive node—or a small multi-node local cluster—partitioned into four decoupled planes that map onto src/nectr/services/:

| Architectural Plane | Core Component | Recommended OSS Stack & License Status | Role in 2+ Hive Federation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Consensus & State | Local Hive Chain & Contracts | Python PoUW-PoW Engine \+ RocksDict (Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause/MIT) or aiosqlite (MIT)6 | Deterministic verification of tutoring attestation roots, escrow state, and Accepted Status transitions. |
| Hexagonal Service Layer | HiveServiceLayer (Relayer, Escrow Coordinator, Bridge, KG Telemetry) | fastapi, uvicorn, httpx, Python stdlib asyncio (upstream FastAPI/Uvicorn/HTTPX licenses unverified in retrieved sources) | Exposes HTTP/REST ports and orchestrates outbound adapters; avoids obsolete asyncio PyPI backport8. |
| Cross-Hive Federation | Outbound Relayer & Proof Bus | nats-server \+ nats-py Leaf Nodes & JetStream Domains (Apache-2.0)9 | Bridges Accepted Status proofs across asymmetric campus NATs via outbound port 7422 links and stream mirrors12. |
| Off-Chain Read Model | Knowledge Graph Telemetry | Event-sourced consumer consuming committed block logs | Materializes networkx or analytical graph views asynchronously without polluting deterministic consensus state. |
| Testnet & Chaos Plane | Multi-Hive Orchestrator & Fault Injection | Kurtosis (Apache-2.0 post-June-2024) \+ Pumba (Apache-2.0) or Toxiproxy Helm chart (Apache-2.0)4 | Launches reproducible multi-Hive enclaves and injects tc netem latency, packet loss, and TCP disruptions14. |
| Observability & Artifacts | Metrics, Traces & Dashboards | OpenTelemetry Python (Apache-2.0) \+ Prometheus OTLP \+ Perses (Apache-2.0)3 | Captures consensus, PoUW, and bridge latency series for paper figures; Prometheus server license unverified in retrieved sources. |

Cross-hive bridging executes as an asynchronous proof-relay pipeline rather than a synchronous cross-campus lock. When an escrow contract on HIVE\_A transitions to Accepted Status, the consensus engine commits a deterministic state root, block header, and Knowledge Graph attestation root (kg\_root) while emitting a typed post-commit domain event to HIVE\_A's local JetStream domain12. The Cross-Hive Bridge adapter in HIVE\_B's HiveServiceLayer receives the mirrored proof event over an outbound NATS Leaf Node link, verifies the cryptographic proof locally, and submits a deterministic settlement transaction to HIVE\_B12.

## **Lightweight P2P Networking and Multi-Hive Federation**

University pilot deployments face two structural networking constraints: campus IT firewalls routinely block arbitrary inbound P2P ports, and nectR's HiveServiceLayer already commits to Python's standard asyncio loop via fastapi, uvicorn, and httpx. The table below compares viable Python-compatible and sidecar federation transports.

| Transport / Consensus Stack | License Status | Async Compatibility (FastAPI/httpx) | Campus NAT / Firewall Traversal | Cross-Hive Accepted Status Fit | Operational Caveats |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| nats-server \+ nats-py (Leaf Nodes \+ JetStream) | Apache-2.09 | Native asyncio (nats-py)9 | High: Leaf nodes dial outbound TLS on port 7422 to a relay hub13 | High: JetStream domains and stream mirrors replicate proofs across outages12 | Practitioner reports note JetStream lacks a built-in dead-letter queue19; distinct domain names required per Hive13. |
| py-libp2p (v0.8.0) | Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-APACHE)20; libp2p MIT/Apache-2.021 | Incompatible in-process: exclusively uses trio, removed asyncio1 | Moderate: AutoNATv2, Circuit Relay v2, WebRTC-Direct1 | Moderate: Native PeerIDs and GossipSub, pre-1.0 interop active22 | Requires separate sidecar process/IPC to isolate trio from uvicorn; GitHub org metadata tags license as Other1. |
| CometBFT \+ Python ABCI 2.0 (pyABCI / xian-abci) | Apache-2.026 | Good via socket/gRPC IPC sidecar (Alesh/pyABCI async ABCI 2.0)28 | Low-Moderate: Validator P2P requires routable ports or VPN overlay | Low for core PoUW-PoW: Enforces Tendermint BFT (\<1/3 faults)31 | Replaces PoUW-PoW chain selection with BFT finality; minor version bumps (0.x.y) are protocol-breaking31. |
| ZeroMQ (pyzmq v26.3.0+) | BSD-3-Clause core33 | Native zmq.asyncio support | Poor: Raw sockets lack NAT traversal or federated identity routing | Low-Moderate: Suited to local IPC or static lab VPNs | Repo includes LGPL (zmq/ssh/forward.py) and MPL (perf) files outside core33. |
| httpx / HTTP2 / gRPC Relay | httpx license unverified in retrieved sources | Native (httpx already used in HiveServiceLayer) | Poor-Moderate: Requires ingress tunnels per campus Hive | Baseline fallback only; no native Python gRPC-gossip library evaluated in sources | Lacks durable store-and-forward spooling across campus partitions without an external queue. |

**Why NATS Leaf Nodes \+ JetStream Best Fit Campus Federation**: According to NATS project documentation, nats-server ships as a single Go binary with no external dependencies that typically uses less than 20 MB of RAM10. Although Synadia proposed relicensing future NATS server releases under BSL in April 2025, Synadia and the CNCF reached a formal settlement on May 1, 2025 transferring trademarks to CNCF and committing to keep both nats-server and nats-py under the Apache-2.0 license11. (Synadia noted it is considering a separate commercial distribution embedding the OSS server11.) Architecturally, NATS Leaf Nodes match university network realities because HIVE\_A and HIVE\_B open strictly outbound connections (default leaf port 7422, distinct from client port 4222, route port 6222, and gateway port 7222\) to a cloud or DMZ hub, authenticating via JWT accounts and .creds files without exposing inbound campus ports12. Giving each campus Hive its own named JetStream Domain prevents storage collisions across the leaf link, while JetStream Stream Mirrors or Sources replicate Accepted Status proofs reliably once intermittent WAN connectivity recovers12.  
By contrast, py-libp2p matured across 2025–2026 (v0.2.0 through v0.8.0 in September 2026), adding persistent identities (FileSystemKeyStore, save\_identity, create\_identity\_from\_seed), WebRTC-Direct, and deterministic pub/sub readiness helpers (wait\_for\_peer(), wait\_for\_subscription())1. However, because py-libp2p explicitly dropped asyncio in favor of trio (\#174, \#301)1, using it alongside FastAPI/uvicorn forces a multi-process sidecar connected over localhost IPC. Similarly, CometBFT (Apache-2.0) offers mature BFT state replication via ABCI 2.0 (FinalizeBlock, vote extensions, and gRPC/socket IPC) with community Python adapters such as Alesh/pyABCI and xian-abci26. While CometBFT is unsuitable for nectR's core PoUW-PoW mining loop because Tendermint consensus replaces longest-chain work with \<1/3-fault validator voting31, it remains a viable optional sidecar if campuses ever add a permissioned cross-hive checkpoint committee. If pyzmq is adopted for local IPC between HiveServiceLayer and a sidecar miner or py-libp2p daemon, packaging scripts should strip zmq/ssh/forward.py (LGPL) and perf examples (MPL) to preserve pure BSD/Apache-2.0 compliance33.

## **Deterministic Embedded State Storage and Knowledge Graph Isolation**

Academic artifact reproducibility requires that replaying a genesis state and ordered block log on two distinct university servers yields bit-for-bit identical state roots. Embedded Python storage engines differ markedly in serialization guarantees, snapshot tooling, and license transparency.

| Storage Engine / Binding | License Status | Access & Concurrency Model | Deterministic Replay Mechanism | Determinism & Operational Risks |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| RocksDict (RocksDB Python binding) | Apache-2.0 / BSD-3-Clause / MIT7 | Single-writer / concurrent readers over embedded LSM-tree | Canonical byte-key ordering \+ immutable checkpoints and Merkle state roots | Secondary encyclopedia metadata describes it as an actively maintained replacement for python-rocksdb39; non-relational KV requires manual indexing; no benchmarks in retrieved sources. |
| SQLite via aiosqlite | aiosqlite MIT6; libsqlite upstream license unverified in retrieved text40 | Single-writer \+ concurrent WAL readers | sqlite3\_snapshot\_open / sqlite3\_snapshot\_recover over WAL41 | Community reports note now() breaks SQL replay determinism42; multi-writer locks and locale collations risk state divergence. |
| py-lmdb (LMDB Python binding) | Unverified in retrieved HPC software catalogs43 | Memory-mapped B+tree, zero-copy reads, strict single-writer | Copy-on-write MVCC pages with read snapshots | Requires pre-sizing memory map; unconfirmed license classification in available university catalog entries requires audit before adoption. |
| Append-Only Log \+ JetStream | Apache-2.0 (nats-server)9 | Sequential immutable log per Hive | Monotonic sequence IDs \+ cryptographic content hashes | Read-only event log; must materialize into RocksDict or SQLite for O(1) contract balance/escrow queries. |

For core chain and contract state (tutoring escrow balances, PoUW difficulty epochs, and Accepted Status registries), **RocksDict** provides the cleanest deterministic substrate when state is encoded as canonical byte keys, eliminating SQL query-planner variability and carrying verified permissive licensing (Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT)7. Where relational queries over escrow timeouts or cross-hive bridge nonces justify SQL ergonomics, **SQLite wrapped by aiosqlite** (MIT) supports crash-consistent WAL snapshot recovery via sqlite3\_snapshot\_open and sqlite3\_snapshot\_recover6. To guarantee deterministic replay in SQLite, the consensus adapter must enforce single-writer sequential block application, ban non-deterministic SQL functions such as now(), CURRENT\_TIMESTAMP, and random()42, derive every timestamp strictly from verified block headers, and specify explicit ORDER BY clauses on any state-hashing query.  
Because no primary benchmarks or license audits covering networkx or embedded Python graph databases were present in the collected sources, nectR should isolate **Knowledge Graph telemetry** as an asynchronous, event-sourced CQRS read model completely outside consensus validation. Following an event pattern analogous to CometBFT's post-commit block event triggers (EventLock, EventCompleteProposal)46, block execution stores only a compact 32-byte Knowledge Graph attestation root (kg\_root) on-chain and appends immutable domain events (AttestationCommitted, EscrowLocked, AcceptedStatusGranted) to the local log. The Knowledge Graph Telemetry service in HiveServiceLayer tails these committed events asynchronously to populate networkx or an off-chain graph store, ensuring that floating-point centrality math, Python runtime upgrades, or graph schema changes never trigger consensus forks.

## **Reproducible Multi-Node Testnets and Empirical Telemetry**

Empirical evaluation for peer-reviewed papers demands deterministic multi-Hive provisioning, repeatable network fault injection, and standardized metric capture without restrictive licensing.

| Tool Category | Candidate Tool | License Status | Capabilities & Ecosystem Fit | Academic Testbed Limitations & Caveats |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Topology Orchestrator | Kurtosis (post-June 2024\) | Apache-2.0 since June 2024 open-sourcing4 | Starlark-packaged reproducible blockchain devnets ("Docker Compose for blockchain") \+ GitHub Actions CI (kurtosis-github-action)4 | Earlier CLI releases (e.g., 1.11.1) used BSL5; project site notes a small contributor base with one full-time maintainer4. |
| Topology Orchestrator | Docker Compose / k3s | Licenses unverified in retrieved sources | Single-host Compose (used in CometBFT quickstarts)32 or multi-VM Kubernetes scheduling | Hand-maintained Compose degrades across multi-campus topologies; no Compose-vs-k3s footprint benchmarks in retrieved sources. |
| Network Chaos | Pumba (v1.2.1, Aug 2026\) | Apache-2.015 | Docker, containerd, Podman tc netem (egress delay, loss, corruption, rate) and iptables (ingress loss)16 | Requires NET\_ADMIN and kernel sch\_netem (fails on Minikube lacking sch\_netem)16; always set \--duration and \--label allowlists16. |
| Network Chaos | Chaos Mesh | Apache-2.056 | CNCF incubating K8s CRDs for network, DNS, HTTP, I/O, kernel, and per-pod clock skew faults56 | Requires Kubernetes cluster and privileged DaemonSet52; unnecessary overhead for single-server Compose runs. |
| Network Chaos | Toxiproxy | Helm chart Apache-2.014; upstream core license unverified in retrieved sources | Userspace TCP proxy injecting latency, rate caps, and resets14 | Unprivileged operation works on locked-down university VMs lacking NET\_ADMIN, but affects proxied TCP connections only. |
| Observability & Dashboards | OpenTelemetry Python \+ Prometheus \+ Perses | OTel Python & Perses Apache-2.03; Prometheus & Grafana licenses unverified in retrieved sources | opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus (Python \>=3.10) \+ Prometheus \--web.enable-otlp-receiver (30m out-of-order window) \+ Perses Grafana dashboard migration3 | Prometheus OTLP receiver requires service.instance.id and service.name for target\_info series18; no PyArrow/Parquet benchmarks in retrieved sources. |

For single-host academic evaluation and CI artifact pipelines, **Kurtosis** (explicitly pinning post-June-2024 Apache-2.0 builds) paired with **Pumba** offers the highest reproducibility4. Each campus Hive (nectr-node, nats-server leaf, HiveServiceLayer, and telemetry sidecar) runs inside isolated Kurtosis enclaves driven by parameterized scripts4. Pumba attaches temporary nettools helper containers to target container network namespaces to inject realistic WAN jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth throttling across cross-hive NATS links, enforcing \--duration caps, \--label target allowlists, and immutable @sha256: image digests16. On locked-down university VMs where sysadmins withhold NET\_ADMIN or sch\_netem kernel modules, **Toxiproxy** proxies TCP links in userspace14, whereas multi-VM Kubernetes pilots requiring isolated container clock-skew faults should deploy **Chaos Mesh**56.  
For structured telemetry, HiveServiceLayer and the consensus worker should instrument PoUW solve/verify times, block intervals, and cross-hive Accepted Status propagation latencies using **OpenTelemetry Python** (opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-exporter-prometheus, Apache-2.0)17. Configuring Prometheus with \--web.enable-otlp-receiver ingests OTLP metrics at /api/v1/otlp/v1/metrics, applies the built-in delta-to-cumulative processor, and handles partitioned Hive delays via storage.tsdb.out\_of\_order\_time\_window: 30m18. **Perses** (Apache-2.0 across all components) provides live visualization and imports existing Grafana dashboards3. Because no primary benchmarks for PyArrow/Parquet export overhead were found in the surveyed material, test runners should query Prometheus and JetStream logs at experiment teardown via a batch script to generate immutable CSV/Parquet artifacts for paper figures.

## **PoUW-PoW Difficulty Coupling, Sybil Resistance, and VM Footprint**

Foundational Proofs of Useful Work (BRSV '17 / CRYPTO '18) by Ball, Rosen, Sabin, and Vasudevan construct PoW challenges from fine-grained complexity problems—Orthogonal Vectors (![][image1]\-OV), 3SUM, and All-Pairs Shortest Paths—where proving requires ![][image2] time (for ![][image1]\-OV with ![][image3]) while verification finishes in ![][image4] time, made non-interactive in the Random Oracle model61. Subsequent transcript-oracle PoUW formalizations provide a direct blueprint for lightweight CPU execution on standard university VMs64.  
Instead of burning cycles on pure SHA-256 nonces (![][image5]65), nectR can couple Knowledge Graph or tutoring attestation verification to difficulty using the transcript-oracle design analyzed in arXiv:2504.09971v464. Given a deterministic challenge seed ![][image6] hashed from the previous block header and current kg\_root, a node executes a bounded useful computation (such as verifying algebraic tutoring attestation matrices or graph-consistency tasks) while recording a compact intermediate transcript ![][image7], then evaluates:  
![][image8]  
where ![][image9] is the oracle output bit-width and ![][image10] (taken as an inverse power of 2\) controls puzzle difficulty64. Crucially for heterogeneous campus VMs lacking GPUs, Remark 5.2 of that analysis identifies two orthogonal difficulty knobs: keeping ![][image10] fixed (e.g., 0.1) while scaling task dimension ![][image11], or fixing ![][image11] to fit VM L2/L3 cache budgets and tuning ![][image10] so provers evaluate more deterministic instances per block64. BRSV further notes (Remark 2.11) that algebraic PoW structure permits distributing prover work across collaborating nodes without amortizing cumulative computational effort62, fitting federated tutoring clusters.  
Game-theoretic equilibrium analysis in arXiv:2606.06700v1 defines the viability boundary for coupling useful work with mining66. Modeling pure mining (![][image12]), pure off-chain useful compute (![][image13]), and joint duplex work (![][image14]), where total security is ![][image15], useful output is ![][image16], and wasted compute is ![][image17], the security surplus above wasted work is:  
![][image18]  
When ![][image19] (meaning ![][image20]), duplex work is strictly dominated and rational participants revert to classical separate PoW and uncoupled computation; when ![][image21] and duplex activity dominates, part of consensus security accrues without wasted compute, while 50% attack costs remain at least as high as classical PoW (![][image22])66. To keep ![][image21] and block shortcuts, nectR must enforce preimage-resistant task functions61, keep proving overhead ![][image23] relative to raw computation64, and bucket task instances into uniform difficulty bands so miners cannot cherry-pick trivial instances67.  
Because modest campus VM clusters have low total CPU hashrate, PoUW-PoW alone cannot stop an external adversary from renting cloud CPUs to overwhelm consensus or farm rewards68. Academic pilots should layer PoUW-PoW with **federated institutional identity gating** modeled on **eduGAIN / Shibboleth** certificate validation69 and privacy-preserving **Zero-Knowledge membership proofs**68. Under this architecture, an institution's identity provider validates campus membership once via signed federation certificates69, and nodes attach unlinkable BBS+ / Groth-Kohlweiss one-out-of-many ZK membership credentials (requiring logarithmic-order verification overhead as shown in Sybil-resistant SSI designs70) alongside PoWFaucet-style rate-limited puzzle thresholds50. For open deployments lacking federated institutional IdPs, secondary collusion controls such as Proof-of-Prestige61 or decentralized mutual biometric and social-graph verification (e.g., De-SyRIS71) mitigate Sybil proliferation without exposing student PII on-chain.

## **Operational Failure Modes and Mitigations in University Pilots**

University-hosted blockchain testbeds fail most frequently due to campus network policies, container runtime mismatches, and non-deterministic execution drift rather than consensus mathematics.

| Failure Mode | Typical Pilot Cause | Architectural Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Asymmetric campus firewall isolation | Campus NATs and IT policies block inbound P2P ports (4222, 30303, 26656), stranding Hives. | Use NATS Leaf Nodes making outbound TLS connections on port 7422 to a relay hub, bridging Accepted Status proofs bidirectionally without inbound firewall rules13. |
| Async event-loop deadlocks | Importing py-libp2p directly into FastAPI/uvicorn workers fails because py-libp2p enforces trio exclusively1. | Standardize on nats-py (native asyncio)9 inside HiveServiceLayer, or isolate py-libp2p in a separate OS container behind localhost IPC. |
| Non-deterministic replay drift | Calling SQLite now()42, Python wall clocks, or embedding floating-point networkx analytics inside block validation causes state-root forks. | Use RocksDict7 or single-writer aiosqlite WAL6 with banned SQL clock functions42; derive timestamps from block headers; isolate networkx off-chain. |
| Chaos tool failure on restricted VMs | Pumba netem aborts on Minikube or hardened university VMs missing sch\_netem or NET\_ADMIN16. | Probe sch\_netem in CI pre-flight; fall back to unprivileged Toxiproxy for TCP fault testing14 or Chaos Mesh on Kubernetes for pod/clock faults56. |
| Ephemeral identities and CI race conditions | Container restarts overwrite random PeerIDs, while arbitrary sleep() calls cause flaky multi-Hive sync tests1. | Persist keys via create\_identity\_from\_seed / .creds volumes1; replace fixed sleeps with explicit readiness hooks (wait\_for\_peer(), JetStream acks)1. |
| Permissive license compliance drift | Pulling older BSL Kurtosis CLIs5, pyzmq's LGPL/MPL helpers33, or unverified/copyleft dashboards breaks artifact rules. | Pin post-June-2024 Apache-2.0 Kurtosis4 and Perses (Apache-2.0)3, strip zmq/ssh/forward.py and perf if using pyzmq33, and enforce CI SBOM checks. |
